Cathedral Basilica of Ayacucho
Built between 1612 and 1672. It is the most important church in the city, famous for its wood-carved and gold-leafed altarpieces.
Visit it at night to appreciate its illumination.
Temple of San Cristóbal
Considered the oldest temple in the city (1540). It has a single tower and a simple but historical architecture.
Key point in the Holy Week processions.
Temple of La Merced
Built in the 16th century, it stands out for its stone facade and side tower. It houses a large bell.
Admire the canvases of the Ayacucho school.
Temple of Santo Domingo
It stands out for its twin towers and gray stone facade. Its architecture is one of the most elegant.
Ideal for photography at sunset.
Temple of San Juan de Dios
Located next to the old colonial hospital. It holds a rich history of charity and faith.
Observe its baroque style main altar.
Temple of San Francisco de Asís
16th-century church that has a valuable colonial library and one of the largest bells in the city.
Visit its library if you have the chance.
Temple of Santa Clara de Asís
Famous for its Mudejar coffered ceiling and golden baroque altarpieces. It was the first monastery in the city.
Don\'t leave without buying sweets from the nuns.
Temple of Santa Ana
Located in the artisans\' neighborhood. It is a very important cultural and religious center for retablo makers.
Visit the nearby artisan workshops.
Temple of Santa María Magdalena
Located in the traditional artisans\' neighborhood of La Magdalena. Simple but imposing facade.
Tour the neighborhood to see Huamanga stone carvings.
Temple of La Compañía de Jesús
Located facing the Main Square. Its imposing pink volcanic stone facade is unique.
Observe the details of the Jesuit carvings.
Temple of Nuestra Señora de Loreto
Located next to La Compañía de Jesús, it stands out for its elegance and baroque details.
Appreciate the harmony of its facade with the surroundings.
Temple of San Agustín
Church with neoclassical and baroque altarpieces. It is highly visited during its festivity in August.
Venerate the image of the Virgin of Consolation.
Temple of San Sebastián
Located in the upper part of the city, it offers a sober architecture and well-preserved altarpieces.
Admire the view of the city from the area.
Temple of Belén
A small and charming colonial church with an atmosphere of great peace.
Ideal for moments of silent prayer.
Temple of Santa Teresa
Monastery of the Discalced Carmelite Nuns. It has an impressive main altarpiece.
Try the traditional sweets at its porter\'s lodge.
Temple of San Francisco de Paula
It features carved altarpieces and colonial canvases that narrate ancient religious stories.
Appreciate the paintings of the high choir.
Temple of La Buena Muerte
Also known as Buen Pastor. It stands out for its simplicity and history linked to charity.
Observe its wood carvings.
Temple of La Amargura
Small temple linked to the devotion of the Stations of the Cross and the moments of reflection during Holy Week.
Visit it during the night processions.
Temple of Carmen Alto
Located in the historic muleteers\' district, a strategic point of culture and faith.
Try typical gastronomy in the nearby market.
Temple of Pampa San Agustín
Historic chapel that represents popular faith in the peripheral areas of the center.
Observe its colonial rural architecture.
Temple of San Juan Bautista
Main church of the San Juan district, center of great popular celebrations.
Enjoy the festivities in the main square.
Temple of Soquiaqato
Located in one of the most traditional neighborhoods, center of the festivity of the Lord of the Sentence.
Ideal to experience Ayacucho neighborhood faith.
Temple of Conchopata
Small chapel near the archaeological zone, surrounded by pre-Inca and colonial history.
Visit the nearby pottery workshops.
Temple of El Calvario
It symbolizes the way of the cross and offers a panoramic view of Huamanga.
Place of pilgrimage on Good Friday.
Temple of Nuestra Señora del Pilar
Chapel dedicated to the Virgin of the Pillar, with simple and cozy architecture.
Appreciate the tranquility of its interior.
General Cemetery Chapel
Dedicated to eternal rest and prayer for the deceased.
Visit the chapel on All Saints\' Day.
Temple of Señor de Quinuapata
Traditional neighborhood church with a very picturesque square.
Enjoy the tranquility of the neighborhood.
Temple of Capillapata
Emblematic church that underwent reconstruction to preserve its colonial structure.
Observe the historical restoration efforts.
Temple of Señor de Arequipa
Small church of deep faith, highly attended by the locals in the area.
Ideal place for meditation.
Temple of Virgen del Rosario de Chiquinquirá
Dedicated to the patron saint of Colombia, but with a strong tradition in Huamanga.
Appreciate the local religious art.
Temple of Virgen de Fátima
Modern chapel dedicated to the Virgin of Fatima, a center of Marian devotion.
Attend Sunday mass.
Temple of Señor de las Maravillas
Modern temple that welcomes a large number of faithful during its annual festivities.
Visit it during its patron saint festivities.
Temple of Señor de Pampa Cruz
Located in an elevated area, it is a reference point for the faithful of the sector.
Enjoy the view from outside the temple.
Huaraca Forest
A beautiful Andean forest ideal for hiking, photography, and connecting directly with the nature of Vinchos.
Chapalla Andean Cenote
Impressive natural formation hidden in the Andes, surrounded by unique rock formations and landscapes.
Intiwarkuna Viewpoint
Natural viewpoint from where you can see the entire city of Huamanga and its surroundings with panoramic landscapes.
Qorihuillca Crevasses
Narrow rock formations that create canyon-like passages. Perfect place for adventure tourism and photography.
Campanayuq Rural Waterfalls
Small natural waterfalls formed by runoff and rains in rural areas, surrounded by local vegetation.
Enchanted Route of the Condors
Andean route that crosses mountainous landscapes where you can observe condors in their natural habitat and traditional communities.
Quinua Nature Trails
Alternative routes among Andean fields and rural landscapes that allow you to enjoy nature away from mass tourism.
Piquimachay Natural Zone
Natural landscape with prehistoric caves and mountainous areas, ideal for exploration and uncrowded walks.
Yanacocha Lagoon (Ayacucho)
High Andean lagoon of dark waters surrounded by pastures and mountains. It is a quiet place rarely visited by tourists.
Campanayoq Hill
Mountainous formation with panoramic views and natural remains. Ideal for trekking and exploration.
Muyu orqo
Natural gorge with rock formations and Andean vegetation, rarely frequented by visitors.
Paqcha Chirapaq Waterfall
Beautiful waterfall whose name in Quechua means \'rainbow waterfall\'. It is a quiet place surrounded by native vegetation and rock formations.
The Swamp (El Pantano)
Natural wetland of great historical importance located near the Historical Sanctuary of the Pampa de Ayacucho. It is an ecosystem that houses migratory birds and native flora.
Hatun Condoray

A natural viewpoint and archaeological site of Wari-Chanka origin. It is famous for being one of the best spots in the region for adventure sports and for its rock formations that offer a spectacular view of the valley.
Rosas Pampa de Vinchos
Vast Andean plains with open landscapes and mountain views, ideal for disconnecting from urban noise.
Qosniccpaccha Waterfall

Its name means \'smoking waterfall\' due to the mist it generates when impacting from its more than 100 meters of height. It is a destination of pure adventure, with a path that crosses impressive crevasses, rivers, and rock formations.
Uchkuera
Noted for offering experiences that combine impressive Andean landscapes with cultural immersion.
Uchillki Lagoon

A serene lagoon of calm waters located in the southern circuit of Ayacucho. It is an ideal destination for ecotourism where you can enjoy water activities surrounded by an impressive Andean landscape and unique rock formations.
Puya Raimondi Forest - Manallasacc

Extensive forest that houses thousands of specimens of the Puya Raimondi (Titanka), the largest inflorescence in the world. It is a high mountain ecosystem where these ancient plants bloom only once in their lifetime before dying.
Niñoyujay Hot Springs
Natural pools of thermo-medicinal waters rich in minerals. It is a rustic and quiet place, surrounded by Andean landscapes, ideal for resting and relieving muscle or joint ailments.
Acuchimay Viewpoint
From this natural viewpoint you have a panoramic view of the entire city of Huamanga. It is an emblemati place with monuments and green areas.
Pumapaqcha Waterfall

Its name in Quechua means \'waterfall of the puma\'. It is an impressive cascade of crystal clear waters descending between unique rock formations. It is considered a sacred place of purification by locals.
Huatatas
Warm and picturesque valley known for its pleasant climate and gastronomic offer. It is the favorite place to enjoy typical dishes outdoors, surrounded by fruit orchards and the Huatatas River.
Dwelling of the Apus (Morada de los Apus)

Impressive theme park of giant sculptures carved in stone. The works represent Andean deities, mystical figures, and the worldview of ancient Peruvians, creating a magical atmosphere in the middle of the mountain.
Belén Temple Atrium Viewpoint

Located in the traditional neighborhood of Belén, this viewpoint offers an exceptional panoramic view of the city of Ayacucho and the surrounding hills. The 17th-century temple stands out for its stone architecture and historical importance in local faith.
Wari Archaeological Complex

Ancient capital of the Wari Empire (7th to 13th centuries). It is an immense pre-Hispanic stone city where sectors such as Monjachayuq and Cheqo Wasi stand out. Its walls up to 12 meters high and advanced canal system reflect the greatness of this culture.
Puncupata Viewpoint

A spectacular natural balcony located in the highlands of the city. Its name means \'upper part of the door\', and it offers a 360-degree view of the entire Huamanga valley. It is a favorite place to watch the sunset and enjoy the fresh air.
Infiernillo Cave

Impressive rock formation and deep natural cavern. Its name comes from the darkness and mysterious air currents that emanate from its interior. It is a site of archaeological and geological interest where stalactites and whimsical formations can be seen.
Occochaca Waterfall

Beautiful waterfall of crystal clear water surrounded by lush vegetation and rock formations. It is a perfect place to connect with nature, where the sound of the water and the singing of the birds create an atmosphere of absolute peace.
Turquoise Waters of Millpu
Spectacular turquoise natural pools formed along a canyon, considered one of the most beautiful natural jewels of Ayacucho.
Adoration of the Christ Child and Huaylijía and Huera dances
Andean Christmas tradition where the Child Jesus is worshiped with typical dances like the huaylía, highlighting religious fervor and native music.
Bring a camera to capture the colorful clothing of the dancers and arrive early at the downtown churches.
Descent of the Kings
Commemoration of the arrival of the Three Wise Men with processions through the main streets, accompanied by chants and biblical representations.
It is a very family-friendly event; ideal for enjoying the local gastronomy offered around the Main Square.
Feast of San Sebastián
Tribute to the martyr Saint Sebastian. It includes solemn masses and a traditional procession through the neighborhood of the same name, rescuing ancient customs.
Do not forget to try the traditional punch usually handed out by the mayordomos during the eve.
Feast of the Virgin of Candelaria
Marian festivity of great importance that unites Catholic faith with Andean mysticism through prayers and marching bands.
Participate in the preceding novenas to better understand the deep religious roots of this celebration in the region.
Staging of María Parado de Bellido\'s Execution
Patriotic event recreating the sacrifice of the Ayacucho heroine in the Main Square, remembering her bravery for independence.
Arrive early to get a spot near the main stage and better appreciate the theatrical performance.
Carnivals
National Cultural Heritage. Characterized by playing with water, talcum powder, and comparsas (troupes) singing satirical and joyful songs throughout the city.
Wear clothes you don\'t mind getting dirty and protect your electronic devices with waterproof bags.
Patronal Feast of the Lord of Untuna
Central religious event in Lucanas devoted to the image of the Lord of Untuna with masses, processions, and communal fairs.
It is a good opportunity to discover the landscapes of the Lucanas province and its livestock culture.
Feast of the Crosses
Communities bring the crosses down from the tutelary hills to the temples to be blessed, in a ritual symbolizing crop protection.
Wear sunscreen and a hat, as many activities take place in open spaces and along trails.
Feast of the Virgin of Fatima
Spiritual celebration with public prayers and nocturnal processions illuminated by candles, creating an atmosphere of peace and devotion.
Respect the silence during moments of prayer and enjoy the artistic illumination of the churches.
Feast of San Juan
The Feast of San Juan in Ayacucho, celebrated on June 24, is a mix of religious fervor and Andean tradition, standing out especially in the San Juan Bautista district.
Enjoy the puca picante festival, chicharrón, artisan fairs, and cultural activities by visiting local churches and supporting local producers.
Corpus Christi
Solemn procession of the Blessed Sacrament, a celebration of deep faith and Andean syncretism, connected to the great feast of the Lord of the Ascension.
It is essential to see the scissors dancers, who are strongly linked to religious celebrations in the Lucanas province.
Feast of the Virgin of Carmen
Among handkerchiefs, dances, and promises, Huamanga surrenders to the feet of its Mamacha Carmen, patroness of Ayacucho folklore.
Don\'t miss the main procession that usually leaves from the Santa Teresa Temple, where the image is carried on a litter by the brotherhood.
Patronal Feast of Santiago
\'Tayta Shanti\' is celebrated with cattle branding and ritual songs, giving thanks for the reproduction of animals and prosperity.
If you visit a rural estate, respectfully participate in the toast with chicha de jora offered by the cattle owners.
National Holidays, Bulls and Waqrapukus
A combination of national civics and local traditions. The sound of the waqrapukus (horn trumpets) announcing the bullfights stands out.
Visit the Pampa de la Quinua during these days to live a complete historical and cultural experience.
Feast of the Virgin of the Snows
Iconic celebration in Coracora that includes the impressive \'Ingreso de Chamiza\' (burning of dry bushes) and grand bullfighting shows.
Prepare for low nighttime temperatures and make sure to book transportation in advance, as the flow of travelers is very high.
Herranza Ritual or Cattle Branding
Ancestral ceremony of gratitude to the earth where colored ribbons are placed on the cattle, accompanied by tinya and violin music.
Pay close attention to the symbolism of the ribbon colors; each family has its own identity.
Feast of the Virgin of the Assumption
Important agricultural and religious fair that boosts the local economy, celebrated with typical dances and dishes based on alpaca and lamb meat.
It is the ideal place to buy high-quality dairy products and wool textiles at producer prices.
Procession of San Isidro Labrador
The patron of farmers roams the streets blessing the ox yokes and work tools to ensure a good harvest.
Appreciate the decoration of the yokes, which are usually adorned with the best fruits of the season.
Feast of San Bartolomé
Central festivity in Cangallo highlighting the culture of the Morochucos, brave horsemen who perform feats on horseback in the pampas.
Do not miss the horse races; they are the main event and showcase the great skill of local riders.
Patronal Feast of San Miguel
Celebration in the VRAEM area that integrates elements of the jungle and highlands, with colorful parades and coffee and cocoa exhibitions.
Take the opportunity to visit the nearby waterfalls and enjoy the warm climate of the tropical zone.
Yarqa Aspi or Irrigation Ditch Cleaning
Festive community work where irrigation canals are cleaned to receive rainwater, accompanied by dances and shared food.
It is a unique experience of Andean coexistence; politely ask for permission to share the table with the community members.
Feast of the Lord of Quinuapata
Traditional neighborhood celebration in Huamanga that keeps faith alive with prayers, firework castles, and civil music bands.
Visit the neighborhood market during these days to taste the most authentic homemade seasoning in the city.
Water Festival
Ritual of gratitude to the springs and water sources, fundamental to the Andean worldview and agriculture in the Lucanas province.
Listen to the elders\' stories about the origin of the springs; they are fascinating tales about respect for nature.
Feast of the Virgin of Las Mercedes
Tribute to the Grand Marshal of Peru. Includes military and religious parades, highlighting the solemnity and respect for the patroness of arms.
Observe the elegance of the procession, which is usually accompanied by the police or army music band.
Patronal Feast of San Francisco
Celebration highlighting humility and love for animals, typical of the Franciscan order, with liturgical activities and popular fairs.
It is a good moment for reflection and to enjoy the colonial architecture of the local churches.
All Saints\' Celebration
Tradition of visiting cemeteries bringing music and food. In Ayacucho, the baptism of tantawawas (baby-shaped breads) is fundamental.
Visit artisanal bakeries to buy the best tantawawas and bread horses.
Ayacucho Folklore Day
Artistic gala featuring the best music and dance groups of the region, celebrating Ayacucho\'s rich cultural heritage.
Look for the schedule at the UNSCH Cultural Center to attend Ayacucho guitar concerts.
Anniversary of the Battle of Ayacucho and Tusuy and Nichik Dance
Commemoration of the victory on the Pampa de la Quinua. Includes the warrior dance of tusuy and nichik representing the soldiers\' courage.
Bring warm clothes and sunscreen; the weather on the pampa can quickly change from intense sun to cold wind.
Procession of the Virgin of Sorrows
The procession of the Virgin of Sorrows in Ayacucho is a central act of faith, especially highlighting Friday of Sorrows and Good Friday.
It is recommended to bring candles, warm clothes for the night, and arrive early around the square to observe the floral carpets.
Palm Sunday
Triumphal entry of Jesus. The faithful flock to churches with woven olive palms to be blessed, marking the start of Ayacucho\'s Holy Week.
Buy your palms early around the Main Square and enjoy the festive yet solemn atmosphere.
Holy Week: Easter Sunday
The most important religious festivity in Peru. It culminates with the majestic procession of the Risen Christ on an immense litter illuminated by thousands of candles at dawn.
Wake up early (4:00 AM) to find a spot in the Main Square and witness the litter leaving the Cathedral. It is an unforgettable sight.
Anniversary of the Foundation of Huamanga
Civic and cultural celebration for the Spanish foundation of the city. Includes parades, serenades, and gastronomic fairs.
Participate in the serenade the night before in the Main Square and enjoy live Ayacucho music.
Hipólito Unanue Regional Historical Museum
The main museum of Ayacucho, created in 1946. It presents 15,000 years of history, from the Pikimachay Cave findings to the colonial era.

Located in the Simón Bolívar Cultural Center, this Ministry of Culture museum has five permanent rooms. The first room addresses Andean prehistory with findings from the Pikimachay Cave: lithic tools, extinct fauna bones, and plant remains from 20,000 years ago. The second room presents the Wari Culture (500–1100 AD), the first major urban civilization of the Andes, with polychrome ceramics, textiles with four-pointed caps, and scale models of the 2,000-hectare walled metropolis. The third room exhibits Wari daily life and the subsequent Chanka Culture. The fourth and fifth rooms show colonial and historical-artistic art: viceregal paintings, Huamanga stone sculptures, and historical documents. Hours: Tuesday to Sunday.
Wari Site Museum
Inaugurated in 1996 next to the Wari Archaeological Complex, it exhibits ceramics, lithics, textiles, and monoliths from site excavations.

The Wari Site Museum is located at km 23 of the Ayacucho–Quinua highway. It is the gateway to the Wari Monumental Archaeological Complex, capital of the first pan-Andean culture (500–1100 AD). The museum exhibits pieces recovered in excavations: Conchopata-style ceramics with representations of the Staff God, carved lithics, textiles with geometric designs, monoliths, and metal objects. Explanatory panels describe the urban organization of the site, which had differentiated neighborhoods, temples, artisan workshops, and hydraulic systems. Administrated by the Ministry of Culture of Peru.
Quinua Site Museum – House of the Capitulation
Inaugurated on December 9, 1974, it commemorates the Battle of Ayacucho of 1824. It exhibits weapons, uniforms, and the room where the independence of South America was sealed.

Located in the main square of the town of Quinua, 35 km from Ayacucho. It commemorates the sesquicentennial of the battle that consolidated the independence of South America. Its rooms exhibit weapons of the era (rifles, sabers, cannon models), uniforms of the royalist and patriot armies, strategic maps, and paintings illustrating the battle. The highlight is the room where General José de Sucre and Viceroy La Serna signed the Capitulation of Ayacucho on December 9, 1824. Quinua is also famous for its ceramics, with typical clay churches on the rooftops.
Mariscal Andrés A. Cáceres Historical Museum
Located in the Vivanco Colonial House (17th century), with rooms dedicated to the hero of the Pacific War. It features unique limestone arches and Cusco School paintings.

Occupying the Vivanco House built between 1640 and 1700, this is one of the best-preserved colonial mansions in Ayacucho. The entrance leads to a courtyard with artistic stone paving forming diamonds, human figures, and animals. The stable is unique in Peru: two rows of five limestone arches. The rooms exhibit photographs of Cáceres, Pacific War weapons, personal objects, uniforms, coins, and the reproduction of his bedroom. It also houses canvases from the Cusco and Ayacucho schools. Administrated by the Peruvian Army.
ANFASEP Memory Museum – So that it does not happen again
Peru\'s first memory museum, inaugurated in 2006. It documents the 1980–2000 internal armed conflict with testimonies, photographs, and art.

Built by ANFASEP (National Association of Relatives of the Kidnapped, Detained and Disappeared of Peru), founded in 1983 by mothers and wives of the disappeared. The first room recreates a torture chamber and a grave, with sculptures symbolizing the violence. The second room exhibits photographs of the disappeared, victims\' clothing, and the organization\'s original banner. The third room shows the historical timeline of the conflict. The exterior displays murals up to 9 meters representing episodes of violence. The artisan shop sells retablos and textiles made by the members.
Joaquín López Antay House Museum
House and workshop of the master retablo maker Joaquín López Antay (1897–1981). Shows the life and work of the creator of the modern Ayacucho retablo.

Joaquín López Antay transformed the traditional \"San Marcos\" into a narrative folk art of universal projection. In 1975, he received the National Culture Prize, sparking a historical debate on the value of popular art. His house-workshop in the Santa Ana neighborhood displays original retablos from different periods of his life, photographs, and the workshop where he created his works. Guides explain the process of making the retablo: the wooden box, the potato dough, and the hand-painted plaster figures that narrate Andean life.
The House of the Retablo – Master Silverio Ataucusi
Gallery-workshop of the master retablo maker Silverio Ataucusi Sulca. Exhibits traditional retablos and offers live workshops on the creation process.

A living space where Master Silverio Ataucusi and his family maintain the Ayacucho retablo tradition. The retablo is a two-story wooden box representing religious and traditional scenes using hand-painted potato paste figures. The ground floor exhibits retablos of different themes: livestock, Holy Week, carnivals, and patron saint festivals. Visitors can observe the different stages of production. Recommended to reach by taxi from the Main Square (approx. 15 min).
San José de Quinua Textile Museum
Displays the pre-Columbian textile tradition of the Quinua communities. Textiles are made on backstrap looms using alpaca, cotton, and sheep wool.

This museum documents the pre-Columbian textile activity still alive in the area. Backstrap loom weaving (callhua) is a technique dating back thousands of years. Artisans create blankets, ponchos, and bags using techniques like tapestry and brocade. Designs reproduce iconography of pre-Hispanic origin: diamonds, animal figures, and agricultural scenes with natural colors obtained from plants and minerals. The museum shows the complete process: shearing, washing, spinning, natural dyeing, and weaving.
Vilcashuamán Site Museum
Next to the Inca Complex of Vilcashuamán (15th century). Exhibits Inca lithic pieces, ceramics, and textiles, explaining the importance of this administrative center.

Vilcashuamán (\"Sacred Falcon\") was one of the most important administrative centers of the Tahuantinsuyo, founded by Inca Pachacútec. The site museum exhibits pieces recovered in excavations: imperial-style Inca ceramics, carved stones, textiles, and metal objects. Explanatory panels describe the main sectors: the Ushnu (ceremonial pyramid), the Temple of the Sun and Moon, Pachacútec Square, and the Kallanka palace. The museum visit complements the tour of the surrounding archaeological complex.
Civic-Religious Museum – Ayacucho Cathedral
Located in the Cathedral Basilica of Ayacucho (17th century). Exhibits colonial sacred art, Cusco School paintings, and liturgical ornaments.

The Cathedral, built between 1612 and 1672, is the city\'s most important temple. Its museum houses a valuable collection of colonial sacred art. Highlights include Cusco School paintings from the 17th and 18th centuries representing the Virgin and saints. The collection includes liturgical ornaments embroidered in gold and silver thread, chalices, silver monstrances, and processional sculptures in carved wood. The temple itself, with its golden altarpieces, is an integral part of the visit.
Ayacucho Museum Café
A cultural space in the historic center combining a café and gallery. Exhibits historical photographs, local crafts, and contemporary art.

A multifunctional cultural space located in the heart of the historic center. It combines a café with temporary and permanent exhibitions of historical photographs documenting Ayacucho\'s transformation since the late 19th century. The walls display local crafts—retablos, textiles, ceramics—and works by contemporary Ayacucho artists. It is an ideal starting point for tourists; the staff can provide guidance on tours and artisan workshops. The menu offers local products like chocolate and highland coffee.
Pampa de la Quinua Historical Sanctuary – Site Museum
At the site of the Battle of Ayacucho (Dec 9, 1824). Exhibits panels, models, and military objects next to the 44-meter Obelisk.

The Pampa de la Quinua is the stage where patriot troops defeated the royalist army in the last great battle of South American independence. The site museum exhibits panels with strategic maps, models of the battlefield, period weaponry (bayonets, muskets), uniforms, and flags. A section explains the composition of the armies and the military leaders. The 44-meter commemorative Obelisk is a landmark that can be climbed for panoramic views of the plain. The area is a protected National Sanctuary.
Boza and Solís Mansion
17th-century colonial mansion in the historic center. Displays Cusco School paintings, colonial furniture, and typical Huamanga architecture.

One of the best-preserved colonial mansions in Ayacucho\'s historic center. Built in the 17th century, it exhibits typical Huamanga domestic architecture with its cobblestone courtyard, stone arches, and carved wooden balconies. The rooms display Cusco School paintings, viceregal furniture, and historical documents. It is a living testimony of Huamanga\'s splendor during the Viceroyalty when the city was a key administrative and commercial hub between Lima and Cusco.
Pikimachay Cave and Site Museum
Evidence of some of the oldest human presence in South America (20,000 BC). Exhibits replicas of Paleolithic tools and extinct fauna bones.

Pikimachay (\"Flea Cave\") was excavated in the 1960s, revealing evidence of human occupation dating back to 20,000 BC. It is one of the most important archaeological sites in South America for studying the settlement of the Americas. Findings include Andean Paleolithic stone tools, bones of extinct animals like mastodons and saber-toothed tigers, and plant remains. The site museum presents replicas of these findings with explanatory panels on the archaeological research process and the life of the region\'s first inhabitants.
ViaVia Cafe Ayacucho

The favorite restaurant on the Main Square. Peruvian and international cuisine with an unbeatable view of the Huamanga Cathedral. Specialty in quinoa chaufa, natural juices, Belgian beers, and vegetarian/vegan options.
Sukre Cocina Peruana

High-class restaurant facing the Main Square. Fusion of regional Ayacucho cuisine with modern techniques. Famous for its Huamanguino-style chicharrón, corn-crusted trout, and an elegant menu of Latin American dishes.
Restaurante La Huamanguina

The ultimate reference for Ayacucho cuisine in the city, located on the second floor of Jr. Asamblea. Its Puca Picante is considered the best in Ayacucho. Offers artisanal macerated drinks of lemon balm, wayramuña, and passion fruit.
Restaurante Las Flores

Spacious typical Ayacucho cuisine restaurant on Jr. Olaya, very popular among locals. Stands out for its roasted pork, Huamanguino chicharrón, and a huge variety of artisanal macerated drinks. View of the Main Square.
El Nino Restaurant

Peruvian and Italian cuisine restaurant near the Main Square. Beloved by locals and tourists alike. The owner, Niño, attends personally. Specialty in grilled trout, rotisserie chicken, pizzas, and live music on weekends.
Mestizo Restaurante & Café Lounge

Traditional and modern Peruvian fusion restaurant on Jr. Cuzco, 2 blocks from the Main Square. Contemporary colonial atmosphere with a garden. Executive menu for 15 soles. A Michelin pre-star candidate according to reviews.
Fuziones Restaurante

Signature cuisine with organic and hydroponic ingredients. The best meat cuts in the city. Located 3 blocks from the Main Square in a charming alley. Its Tacu Tacu Lomo and Ribeye Steak are visitor favorites.
Magia Negra Taberna Trattoria

The best pizzeria in Ayacucho according to multiple reviews. Bohemian tavern-bar atmosphere with dark and rock decor. Offers artisanal pizzas, craft beers, sangria, pastas, and infusions. Ideal for groups of friends.
Koi – Cocina Nikkei

The only Nikkei (Japanese-Peruvian fusion) restaurant in Ayacucho. Offers tiraditos, stuffed causas with local ingredients, sushi with Andean trout, and Nikkei-style ceviches. One of the highest-rated restaurants in the city.
La Casona Restaurant Turístico

Tourist restaurant in a colonial mansion on Jr. Bellido, one of the best-known in the city for travelers. Extensive menu of typical Ayacucho and Creole dishes. Colonial atmosphere with an inner courtyard and live music on certain days.
Las Tinajas Chicken & Grill

Restaurant with a privileged view of the Main Square. Specialty in wood-fired rotisserie chicken and grills. Juicy chicken with freshly made fries. Very crowded, arriving early is recommended. Lemongrass lemonade is a must.
Restaurant KIBO

Spacious restaurant 5 minutes from the center, in a quiet residential area. Offers a daily typical menu and an extensive à la carte menu. Always full of locals, a sign of its quality and price. A favorite for family lunches.
Restaurante Carbón y Vino

Located in a charming old mansion with gardens and diverse spaces. The ideal place for family breakfast or lunch. Succulent charcoal-grilled meats, puca picante, and selected wines. Warm and cozy atmosphere.
Planta Lovers

The main vegan and vegetarian restaurant in Ayacucho, facing the Main Square. Exclusive plant-based catalog with smoothies, bowls, salads, and meat-free dishes. The healthiest alternative in the historic center.
Retablo – Pollos a la Brasa
Specialists in grilled chicken and steakhouse meats. Very popular in the María Parado de Bellido neighborhood. Delivery available. The best hamburgers and anticuchos in the sector. Family atmosphere.
Puka\'s Wasi

Chifa-Peruvian cuisine restaurant with excellent tiradito. Fusion of Chinese techniques with Andean ingredients: seafood chaufa, wonton soup with mint, and lomo saltado. The quinoa chifa with bean sprouts is a hit.
Antaqa Café de Especialidad

The coziest specialty coffee shop in Ayacucho. Serves 100% single-origin coffee from the VRAEM (Apurímac and Ene River Valley), artisanally roasted. Artisanal breakfasts, homemade pastries, and hot Ayacucho chocolate.
Patio Colonial

Contemporary Peruvian cuisine restaurant in the heart of the historic center. Open colonial courtyard with flowers and viceregal architecture. Signature dishes with local ingredients: Ayacucho river trout, native quinoa, and native potatoes.
Tu Casa Restaurante
Typical Ayacucho breakfast and lunch restaurant, popular among locals. Famous for Huamanguino mondongo (tripe and white corn dish) and artisanal Huamanguino chorizo. Fast service, family atmosphere.
Quinta Recreo Cameycar

One of the restaurants with the best food in all of Ayacucho, near the Acuchimay Viewpoint. Specialty in Peruvian highland dishes: cuy chactado, pachamanca, and puca picante. Attended by city tours and tourist transport. Open-air country estate atmosphere.
